# ScrollFrame

- Inherits [`UIObject`](uiobject.md)
- Created with `Instance.new("ScrollFrame")`

A `Frame` whose contents can be larger than it is (§2.2). It clips its descendants whatever `ClipsDescendants` says -- a scrolling region that did not clip would not be one.

**Members below are the ones this class DECLARES.** Everything its base
offers is on the base's page, which is what keeps one added member on
`Instance` from being a change to every page here.

## Properties

| Name | Type | Default | Access | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CanvasPosition` | `Vector2` | `Vector2.zero` | read/write | How far the canvas is scrolled, in pixels. Clamped to what the canvas allows on the next layout, so a write past the end settles at the end rather than showing emptiness. |
| `CanvasSize` | `UDim2` | `UDim2.new()` | read/write | How big the scrollable area is. Children lay out against this rather than against the frame's own size. |
| `ScrollBarThickness` | `number` | `12` | read/write | In pixels; zero draws no bar and still scrolls, which is what a touch surface wants.<br><br>A bar appears only on an axis that can actually move: a canvas that fits its region gets none, because a bar for an axis with nowhere to go is a bar that lies. The thumb is as long a fraction of the track as the view is of the canvas, and never shorter than the bar is wide -- a thumb of two pixels in a very long canvas is a thumb nobody can grab.<br><br>Both parts take their colour from the frame's own `BackgroundColor`, at a quarter and three quarters alpha. v1 has no theme, and a hard-coded grey would be wrong on half of them.<br><br>The bar is drawn OUTSIDE the region's own clip, or it would scroll away with the content it reports on. |
